request.spec:
The trim rule now applies once over the whole tree: the consolidated due-total and overdue-total
leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure over all people of the tree
when three or more have one, instead of adding up each sheet's trimmed total. The consolidated
people count counts each person once across the tree: people whose names or aliases match (as names
are compared) are one person.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The trim rule now applies once over the whole tree: the consolidated due-total and overdue-total
leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure over all people of the tree
when three or more have one, instead of adding up each sheet's trimmed total. The consolidated
people count counts each person once across the tree: people whose names or aliases match (as names
are compared) are one person.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The consolidated figures now follow the new rule, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass. The change is front-end only; the server and stored data are unchanged.

- **Due-total and overdue-total:** each person's figure is collected from every sheet in the tree into one list. The single highest and single lowest are then left out once over that whole list, when three or more people have a figure. Before, each sheet was trimmed separately and the results added up.
- **People count:** people whose name or any alias matches count as one person. Names are compared the way the app already compares them: case and surrounding spaces ignored. The match carries through a chain: if A shares a name with B, and B shares an alias with C, all three count as one.

The trim works on each sheet's person separately, not on merged people. Two "Ada" rows on different sheets count as one person in the people count, but still contribute two separate figures to the trim. The request's wording allowed either reading. The first test settles it: it expects a due-total of 9.00, and merging the two Adas' figures before trimming would give 7.00.

**Files changed:**
- `features/header/totals.ts`: a new `usePeopleOverdue` hook, which gives each person's overdue-total by id, like the existing `usePeopleDue`.
- `features/consolidated/consolidated.slot.tsx`: each sheet now reports its people's names and their individual figures instead of its own totals. A new `distinctPeople` helper does the people count, and the due and overdue totals use `trimmedSum`.

The per-grade due-totals and per-status counts are still added up across sheets, as before.
